findings.finding: explanationExcerpt still used a trailing-whitespace regex replace (quadratic on a long whitespace run inside one line); hand-backs feed it uncapped input. FIXED after the review in 644e4dad: trimEnd() plus a 200k-space regression test (the reviewer's own prescribed fix; delta is one line + test).
An unclosed <agent-message> followed by the 'That other Claude session' trailer leaves the trailer in the card.
stripTrailer cuts at the earliest of the two trailer starts; a report quoting one trailer phrase mid-body loses its tail in header-only/unclosed shapes.
findings.suggestion: Cut at the nearest-to-end start. Accepted as follow-up.

findings.finding: from-name regex runs over the whole attribute string so an earlier attribute value could be read as a name (harness-written; display only).

Claim under doubt: A hostile 2 MB record cannot freeze the page. — explanationExcerpt(...) in client/src/lib/missionActivityFeedText.ts:186 uses a trailing-whitespace regex replace per line (quadratic on a long whitespace run). ADDRESSED IN WRITING: pre-existing helper already fed unbounded subrunner reports, human replies and assistant prose before V2; V2 adds no new reachability class. FIXED afterwards in 644e4dad (trimEnd plus a 200k-space test).

Claim under doubt: Hand-back text through the chip-enabled MarkdownText is safe. — Inside MissionBody's FileOpenContext, paths in a peer session's hand-back become file chips that resolve against this task's cwd. ADDRESSED IN WRITING: nothing runs without a click, the viewer is read-only, the V4 evidence gate still applies server-side, the tooltip shows the full path, and peer text is trusted like assistant text (V6 accepted the same reach). Follow-up: switch chips off for origin 'session'.

Claim under doubt: A human message stays a user bubble. — A free-form human sentence that STARTS with 'Another Claude session sent a message' is reclassified. ADDRESSED: accepted as a documented consequence of the anchored fingerprint (AC1 deviation); real harness records always carry the exact header line. Follow-up: require the exact header line.

Claim under doubt: The subrunner pill is honest next to its hand-back. — A hand-back without a task-notification could sit under a Running row. ADDRESSED: real transcripts show the notification follows the hand-back within the same delivery; the row resolves on it. Follow-up if a counter-example appears.

Claim under doubt: Peer strings are fully sanitised. — Sender chip is the raw from attribute sliced to 8 chars; zero-width characters in from-name not stripped. ADDRESSED: React text only, no markup injection; display-spoofing only. Follow-up: restrict sender charset and strip zero-width characters.

The dedent strips exactly two leading spaces from every line of the report, including lines inside fenced code blocks or intentionally indented content. A report containing a code sample loses its indentation and can render with wrong semantics (Python, YAML). It also only handles the 2-space harness indent; a 4-space-indented report keeps stray indentation on half the lines.
findings.suggestion: Strip the indent only from lines at the report's base indentation level, or skip dedenting inside fenced code blocks.

findings.finding: A hand-back whose report body is empty/whitespace is dropped entirely — no card, no notice. The user gets no signal that a subagent replied at all, and the spec's "not a message from you" guarantee silently disappears for that record.
findings.suggestion: Still emit a card with a fallback body (e.g. the notice alone, or "Empty report") rather than returning null.

findings.finding: When the message starts with the header phrase but has no `<agent-message>` envelope, `body` is everything after the first newline — including the English trailer (`That "other Claude session" is an agent working inside this same session…`) that the spec says must be hidden. The envelope path handles it; the header-only path doesn't.
findings.suggestion: Also trim a trailing `That "other Claude session"…` sentence in the header-only path, or exclude text after a blank-line-separated trailer.

findings.finding: The auto-scroll dependency counts raw cards, but the DOM length is now `items.length` after folding. When a card transitions between evidence-only and narrated between polls (artifact reconciled away), the card count can stay constant while the folded/unfolded render changes row count — the re-pin signal is missed. Cosmetic (scroll position), not correctness of content.
findings.suggestion: Include `items.length` (or the result-group membership count) in the dependency string.

findings.finding: The `formatElapsed` tests don't cover the negative-delta or invalid-end-timestamp-returning-null path through `SubrunnerRow.stateMeta` (verb with no duration), nor the `ms < 0` branch — `formatElapsed(undefined, "x")` only covers the missing-start case. A regression that made `stateMeta` throw on `NaN` timestamps would pass the suite.
findings.suggestion: Add a SubrunnerRow case with a non-parseable `subrunnerEndedAt` asserting the verb-only meta (e.g. "finished").  Checked and found sound: the parser correctly refuses tool_result-only content (so quoting the fingerprint in a tool output can't reclassify a record); the bloat anti-ratchet is satisfied (session-parser.ts 842 → 775, siblings extracted); the Run-result grouping is render-time only so `deriveActivityFeed` consumers keep their contract; the subrunner-status text-only requirement (never colour alone) is met and tested; no chat composer / chat- testids are introduced. The E2E drives the real JSONL→parser→reducer→DOM chain and asserts absence of framing text, so it would catch a naive implementation. No security issues: hand-back text flows through the same `MarkdownChunk` renderer as all other transcript markdown, no new sinks.  Overall assessment: the change implements all three spec items with strong behavior-level tests; the findings are low-severity edge cases (indentation stripping, empty hand-back, trailer leakage in the header-only shape). Ship-with-fixes at most; the header-only trailer leak is the only one a user is likely to notice.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: approve

findings.finding: Grouping removes every eligible delivery card but retains only the last one. For example, a feed containing a phase delivery followed by a commit delivery loses the phase statement and its action entirely, because both indices are folded but only the commit survives.
findings.suggestion: Preserve other delivery cards as ordinary feed items, or retain all delivery rows in the result card with the commit last.

findings.finding: Result rows render only `card.text`, while grouping also accepts cards with `textFull`. Those cards lose access to their full statement: the grouped renderer has no expansion control and never renders `textFull`.
findings.suggestion: Keep cards with additional `textFull` content outside the group, or provide an expansion control that renders the full text.

findings.suggestion: Render the running/finished/failed/killed/stopped state in a visible text pill while retaining the type and elapsed-time metadata.  Ship-with-fixes. The main features are implemented, but grouping can discard content and the subrunner status treatment remains incomplete.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
